reason: The cited evidence does not directly study the CoCrFeNiTi alloy. E1 describes tensile testing at a single strain rate, not a range, and does not link mechanisms to properties. E2 is about Cu-Al alloys, not HEAs. E3 simulates a different HEA (CoCrCuFeNi) and finds grain boundary sliding, but does not support the strain-rate or grain-size predictions. E4 tests a different HEA at cryogenic temperature and different strain rates, not supporting the room-temperature predictions. None of the key premises are supported by specific prior evidence on the target alloy.
premises: Dislocation glide and twinning are active deformation mechanisms in the alloy
Grain boundary sliding contributes to deformation
Strain rate influences strength and hardness (lower rate increases them)
Grain size influences ductility (larger grains improve it)
Microstructure (grain size, precipitates) mediates these mechanisms
